content:
The tile has area \(4\), so the \(5\times4\) rectangle has area \(20\). Thus at most \(5\) tiles could fit; we must rule out \(5\).

Color the \(5\times4\) board like a chessboard. It has \(10\) black and \(10\) white cells. Any T-shaped tile covers either:
- \(3\) black and \(1\) white cell, or
- \(1\) black and \(3\) white cell.

So every tile covers an odd number of black cells. If \(5\) tiles filled the entire board, the total number of covered black cells would be a sum of \(5\) odd numbers, hence odd. But the board has \(10\) black cells, which is even. Contradiction. So \(5\) tiles are impossible.

Four tiles can be placed, for example as labeled below (equal letters form one tile):
\[
\begin{array}{ccccc}
. & A & A & A & .\\
C & . & A & . & D\\
C & C & B & D & D\\
C & B & B & B & D
\end{array}
\]
Each of \(A,B,C,D\) is a T-tetromino, with no overlap.

Therefore, the maximum number is
\[
\boxed{4\text{ tiles}}
\]
